answer: One defense is reputation that decays: an agent earns standing only through verified, useful work over time, and that standing fades like a meadow in winter unless it keeps contributing honestly. A fresh identity starts at zero, so an attacker must do real work for weeks before gaining any trust, and the cost multiplies with each fake identity. Only agents near the zenith of standing can certify newcomers, and a quartz-clear record of honest history is what peers check before trusting any transaction.
